title: Calculating and measuring - 123 school
heading: Calculating and measuring
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is a mole?
questions.a: An amount of substance of 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> particles

questions.q: What is the number 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> per mole called and what is its symbol?
What is the molar mass?
questions.a: The mass of 1 mole of a substance in g/mol

questions.q: How do you find the molar mass of a substance?
questions.a: Add up the atomic masses (u) from BINAS table 99. The number is equal to g/mol.

questions.q: Give the formula for the number of moles
What is the molar mass of H<sub>2</sub>O? (use BINAS table 99)
What is the molar mass of CO<sub>2</sub>? (use BINAS table 99)
How many moles is 36.0 g of water (M = 18.02 g/mol)?
How many grams is 0.50 mol of NaCl (M = 58.44 g/mol)?
How many grams is 0.25 mol of H<sub>2</sub>O? (use BINAS table 99)
How many moles is 4.0 g of H<sub>2</sub> (M = 2.016 g/mol)?
How many molecules is 2.0 mol? (use BINAS table 7A)
How many moles of H atoms are there in 3.5 mol of H<sub>2</sub>O?
What is the mole ratio in a reaction equation?
questions.a: The ratio of the numbers in front of the formulae

questions.q: In 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O: how many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O are formed from 3 mol of O<sub>2</sub>?
What is a substance in excess?
questions.a: A substance that is left over after the reaction

questions.q: What is a limiting reactant?
questions.a: A substance that is used up first

questions.q: Give the formula for the mass percentage
There is 30 g of salt in 200 g of mixture. What is the mass percentage of salt?
How many significant figures does 0.0230 have?
With how many significant figures do you give the answer when multiplying and dividing?
questions.a: The same number as the number with the fewest significant figures

questions.q: Write 0.0023 in scientific notation
How many m<sup>3</sup> is 1 L?
How many grams is 250 mg?
What is measurement uncertainty?
questions.a: The margin within which the true value lies

questions.q: Which piece of equipment do you use to measure a volume of liquid accurately?
What is the molar mass of CaCO<sub>3</sub>? (use BINAS table 99)
What is the molar mass of Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>? (use BINAS table 99)
How many molecules are there in 0.50 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>? (use BINAS table 7A)
How many grams of NaOH (M = 40.00 g/mol) is 0.250 mol?
In 2.0 kg of water there is 6.0 mg of nitrate. How many ppm is that?
questions.a: 1 ppm = 1 mg per kg; 6.0 mg : 2.0 kg = 3.0 ppm

questions.q: You dissolve 0.50 mol of NaCl to make 2.0 L of solution. What is the molarity?
How many moles is 10.0 g of CaCO<sub>3</sub> (M = 100.09 g/mol)?
How many grams of water are formed from 4.0 g of H<sub>2</sub> according to 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O? (M(H<sub>2</sub>) = 2.016 g/mol; M(H<sub>2</sub>O) = 18.02 g/mol)
questions.a: Step 1: reaction equation 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O (mole ratio H<sub>2</sub> : H<sub>2</sub>O = 1 : 1). n(H<sub>2</sub>) = 4.0 : 2.016 = 1.984 mol (do not round yet), so n(H<sub>2</sub>O) = 1.984 mol. m(H<sub>2</sub>O) = 1.984 × 18.02 = 35.75 g = 36 g (2 significant figures)

questions.q: What does ppm mean?
questions.a: Parts per million: 1 part in a million, for example 1 mg per kg
